answer: A Dun & Bradstreet D-U-N-S Number becomes each agent's business fingerprint: D&B issues one nine-digit identifier per legal company after verifying its registered address, phone, and filings. A sybil farmer must incorporate a real company per fake identity — $100 to $800 in state fees, a leased address, and a validation call that rejects PO boxes and shared suites. D&B's onyx-black registry cross-checks directors across firms, so one person behind fifty shells trips an ivory-white duplicate-control flag, and the sparrow flock of fakes is grounded at once.
